description: Use this when you are the other party to terms a buyer registered. Pass the `terms_id`, your own `continuity_handle` and `business_purpose_statement` true (businesses only); the buyer confirms it with the `agreement_id`. Returns an `agreement_id` naming both parties. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

acceptance_rule.description: What counts as delivered, by when, and who may ask for the finding.

agreement_cancelled.description: Only with agreement_id: either party records that it cancelled the agreement (recorded as that party's statement and published in GAIP's revocation feed).

agreement_id.description: Only on an existing agreement: the buyer confirms business purpose or expert determination, or either party declares a consumer contract.

business_purpose_statement.description: Required true from the seller at acceptance and from the buyer (with agreement_id): you act for purposes relating to your trade, business, craft or profession and the deal is not with a consumer. No finding until both parties have stated it.

consumer_contract.description: true if either party is a consumer: evidence summary only, no finding.

continuity_handle.description: Required: your own continuity handle (continuity_id, token).

finding_mode.description: EVIDENCE_ONLY, or EXPERT_DETERMINATION (needs the buyer's confirmation).

mandate_check_receipt.description: Optional: the gaip_check_mandate receipt you obtained (or {receipt_sha256, state}) if you act for a person; its state is recorded beside the acceptance as a fact and shown in the finding.

seller_key_proof.description: Optional: {jwk, jws over the terms_id, host}; GAIP checks the signature and whether the host published that key.

name: witness_accept_terms
title: Accept registered terms (the other party)
